quick.summary: Why you should never peek at a product test before it finishes.
quick.takeaway: Set a timeline for your test and refuse to look early.

beats.line: My test looks great on day two. Can we just ship it now?
Only if you like flat cakes.
I am not baking. I am running a pricing test.
Same rule. Open the oven too soon, the cake falls flat.
Peek at tests early, you see random noise, not the truth.
This trap is called optional stopping.
Can I just call it quitting early?
Decide the timeline before you start, and wait for it.
So I tell the team we check the numbers on Friday.
Let the oven do its work.

quiz.question: A test looks wildly successful on the second day. What should you do?
options: Wait until the planned end date.
End it immediately to capture the gains.
Tell your manager the good news.
Start a second test alongside it.
quiz.explanation: Results bounce around wildly at first. You must wait for the timeline to end to know if the result is real.

quiz.question: Checking test results early is a reliable way to make faster decisions.
quiz.explanation: Looking early usually just shows you random noise, which leads to bad decisions.
